learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected $160 and locked the best whole-item bag value for capacity fifty kilograms and the three offered items.
observations.exploration: Initial ratio-first bag held ten and twenty kilogram items for $160 with twenty kilograms empty. Attempted thirty kilogram item and received insufficient-space feedback. Removed ten and added thirty, filling capacity for $220. Enabled cutting: ratio-first included ten, twenty and twenty of the thirty kilogram item, totaling $240.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the whole-item answer to $220 and accurately named my best combination. It explained why a two-thirds fraction fills the gap for $240 when cutting is allowed and connected whole-item combinations to dynamic programming.
observations.visual: Inspected inline dark 1257 by 936 screenshots of the full whole-item and fractional bags. Stacked patterned blocks showed twenty plus thirty kilograms for $220, then ten plus twenty plus a clearly labelled twenty-of-thirty segment for $240. Capacity and best whole-item history stayed visible.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884179 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The question tests a plausible greedy optimality claim with a concrete counterexample.
prediction.evidence: Selected the ratio-first result as best.

interaction.reason: Manual packing and a divisibility toggle isolate why the heuristic fails or succeeds.
interaction.evidence: The rejected item, better whole combination and fractional fill expose the constraint.

payoff.reason: The reveal explains the gap and accurately cites the found combination.
payoff.evidence: It distinguishes $220 whole-item optimum from $240 with cutting.

clarity.reason: Weight-proportional blocks and explicit labels explain remaining capacity.
clarity.evidence: The partial item is labelled twenty of thirty kilograms.

transfer.reason: The ending connects the discovered limitation to a concrete algorithm choice and condition.
transfer.evidence: Whole-item combinations motivate dynamic programming, while divisible goods permit ratio-first filling.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Rejecting the best ratio item can improve the total.
surprise.evidence: Twenty plus thirty kilograms beat ten plus twenty by sixty dollars.

visualExplanation.reason: The bag directly exposes wasted capacity and the effect of cutting.
visualExplanation.evidence: The fractional top segment fills the exact gap left by the greedy whole bag.

playfulness.reason: Packing and unpacking forms a small genuine combination puzzle.
playfulness.evidence: The user can test a failing addition and replace items.

practicalValue.reason: It clarifies when a locally best ratio is insufficient.

depth.reason: The lesson includes a condition reversal rather than only a greedy counterexample.
depth.evidence: Allowing cuts restores the ratio rule's optimum.

complexity.reason: Packing is familiar, while ratio optimality and combination search add algorithmic reasoning.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: distinguish local value density from total feasible value.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: three item toggles and a cutting switch.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: A high-ratio choice can block a better combination under indivisibility.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Knapsack optimization and dynamic programming are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Low to moderate: kilograms, dollars, ratios and one fractional item.

whyCool: The same greedy rule changes from misleading to optimal when the items become divisible.
caveat: Only three fixed items and one capacity are available. Dynamic programming is named rather than demonstrated.
missingEvidence: No fresh item set or dynamic-programming process was tested.
